messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — P1: GeoDNS/resolver anomalies detected. Increased NXDOMAIN and inconsistent responses from eu-west resolver pool affecting api.redwood.example.com. Observed via edge-probers and customer telemetry. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geo-dns|geo-dns-triage>. Incident created INC-2026-042.

chris (oncall-sre): ack. I'm on it — pulling dashboards and prober logs now. tagging @nora and @mike.

nora (network): I see spikes in resolver latencies and ~18% NXDOMAIN from Cloudflare resolvers in eu-west-1. Route53 healthchecks are flapping for the eu-west record.

mike (eng-sre): customer impact? any 5xx trends or timeouts reported?

carol (prod): support reports a subset of EU customers seeing 502s and SDK timeouts starting ~02:05Z. Error-rate + retries correlate with the resolver spike window. I'll draft a short status update after we stabilize.

chris (oncall-sre): quick probe — running dig against public resolvers shows intermittent NXDOMAIN. pasting sample:

```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com; sleep 1; done
# outputs: 
# 172.20.10.5
# 
# ;; -> ;; -> NXDOMAIN
# 172.20.10.5
# NXDOMAIN
```

nora (network): confirms inconsistent answers. looks like Cloudflare resolver pool in eu-west is returning stale/invalid records intermittently. Route53's weighted policy is also seeing failing health checks causing rapid weight oscillation.

mike (eng-sre): mitigation options: 1) remove/zero-weight the eu-west RRS in Route53 weighted policy to stop sending new traffic there, 2) open emergency with Cloudflare to remove bad resolver pool, 3) temporarily increase DNS TTL to reduce churn (but that delays rollback). I prefer (1) immediate + (2) parallel.

chris (oncall-sre): executing step (1) now: changing Route53 weighted record for api.redwood.example.com to set eu-west weight=0. Command (dry-run):

```json
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZONE1234 --change-batch '{\n  "Changes": [{\n    "Action": "UPSERT",\n    "ResourceRecordSet": {\n      "Name": "api.redwood.example.com",\n      "Type": "A",\n      "SetIdentifier": "eu-west-1",\n      "Weight": 0,\n      "TTL": 60,\n      "ResourceRecords": [{"Value":"10.11.12.13"}]\n    }\n  }]\n}' --no-cli-pager
```

chris (oncall-sre): applied change — Route53 change-id C1234567890. Change propagated to DNS control plane; TTL is 60s so effects should show up within a minute.

nora (network): opened Cloudflare emergency ticket #CF-8901 and requested they narrow the resolver pool and restart their service in eu-west. sent logs and dig traces.

mike (eng-sre): monitoring metrics — NXDOMAIN rate dropped from 18% -> 2% within 90s after weight shift. Edge prober errors reduced accordingly.

carol (prod): drafting status page: 
"We are experiencing intermittent DNS resolution errors for customers routed through the eu-west resolver pool, causing partial API failures. We have shifted traffic away from the affected region and are monitoring. Some customers may continue to see transient errors while DNS caches propagate."

carol (prod): posting to status.redwood.com in 5.

chris (oncall-sre): also toggled temporary routing policy to favor eu-central pool and verified curl to endpoints returns stable 200s:

```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.example.com/health | jq .
# { "status": "ok", "region": "eu-central" }
```

nora (network): Cloudflare support responded — investigating an internal config rollback they ran at ~02:00Z that coincides with our spike. asked them to expedite rollback or isolate bad nodes.

mike (eng-sre): rolling back any app changes? No app changes required. This is external DNS/resolver-side; app is fine.

chris (oncall-sre): handoff: I'll monitor for another 30m and then pass to nora for longer-term watch. leaving a note: watch NXDOMAIN < 1% and Route53 change status INSYNC.

nora (network): ack, taking over at 03:00Z for monitoring and post-incident followup. I'll keep Cloudflare ticket open and request root-cause timeline.

cloudflare-support: Support update: we've identified a configuration deployment to a subset of eu-west resolver hosts that caused inconsistent cache priming. Rollback in progress; expecting normalization within 5-10 min after rollback completes.

mike (eng-sre): dashboards show resolver errors back to baseline ~03:08Z. No further customer escalations.

carol (prod): final status note draft for customers: 
"Resolved — We mitigated a GeoDNS/resolver inconsistency impacting EU customers by shifting traffic away from the affected pool and coordinating with Cloudflare to rollback a configuration change. Services have returned to normal; we're continuing to monitor and will publish a postmortem with timeline and next steps."

chris (oncall-sre): creating initial postmortem ticket INC-2026-042-PM and assigning to @nora and @mike for RCA and mitigation plan (e.g., add Route53 stability thresholds to prevent oscillation, add automated geo failover cooldown).

nora (network): notes for RCA: investigate why Route53 healthchecks flapped on short-lived failures (healthcheck probe TTL/thresholds), consider backoff/cooldown for weighted policies, and coordinate an SLA call with Cloudflare.

incident-bot: Note: incident still open (status: monitoring). Please update runbook when RCA decisions are made.

carol (prod): closing customer-facing update: posted. will schedule followup once postmortem is ready. :white_check_mark:
